full_judgment: 5. In his Affidavit-in-Reply of 16-8-2007, the petitioner contends that the true facts regarding the opening of the Letter of Credit in 1998 are that both the petitioner as Chairman of the Company along with the Managing Director "jointly signed the relevant Letter of Credit documents" for importation of machineries. It is also submitted that as opposed to the Chairman, it is the Managing Director who has to oversee the daily business of the Company. It is in this regard that the petitioner contends that he duly submitted accounts regarding imported machineries and local purchases to the Managing Director. In yet another Affidavit-in-Reply of 10-2-2007 in addition to reiterating his reservation as to the authenticity of the communication received from Hardmark Engineering as above referred, the petitioner also subsequently questions the authenticity of the BOD resolution adopted on 21-6-2002. In this regard the petitioner alleges that the Company had resolved upon not accepting the petitioner's request for resignation plain and simple and the conditionality of acceptance of such resignation only upon repayment of bank loans has been the product of an afterthought manifested in the text of the resolution being tampered with to read to that effect. In this regard, the petitioner has produced a photocopy of what is asserted to be the text of the original resolution without the interpolation as alleged (Annexure-'F').
